subject: Realtime delivery slowdown affecting live-reply (customer report & follow-up)
messages:
From: Ellie Barnes <ellie@clearline.health>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T08:12:00Z
Subject: Realtime endpoint delayed responses (live chat)

Hi Kimberly,

Over the last hour our support chat has been showing long pauses between tokens — responses either stall for 10–30s or arrive in one big chunk. This is affecting live operator workflows.

We switched to your non-streaming 'complete' endpoint and saw consistent responses, so this looks specific to the streaming path. I attached a small capture of request IDs and timing (customer-logs-20261122.zip).

Can you confirm if this is on your side and if there are any workarounds we should apply while you investigate? We have a billing window at 14:00 PST today and need a contingency plan.

Thanks,
Ellie Barnes
Director, Support Ops
Clearline Health

[attachment: customer-logs-20261122.zip (zip)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Ellie Barnes <ellie@clearline.health>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Realtime endpoint delayed responses (live chat)

Hi Ellie — thank you for the quick heads-up and for the logs. We’re actively investigating and I wanted to give you an immediate status and short-term mitigations: 

1) Triage: Our on-call team is looking at streaming pod metrics and routing logs now. Initial signal shows bursts of high prefix diversity from your tenant that caused transient backpressure in the streaming shard pool.

2) Short-term mitigations you can apply immediately (no code changes required):
  - If acceptable for the billing window, switch temporarily to the non-streaming /v1/complete endpoint (you already tried this with success).
  - As a streaming-specific tweak, reduce client-side max_concurrent_requests to 1 while we stabilize (this reduces multiplexing pressure).
  - As we roll controls, we can pin you to a dedicated route for the next 6–12 hours to avoid cross-tenant microbursts. I can enable that for Clearline if you want us to proceed.

3) Next updates: Marcus is leading the investigation and will reply with a timeline and root-cause hypothesis within the hour.

We’ll keep you posted with concrete steps and will schedule a short call if you prefer live coordination.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

[attachment: mitigation-checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Ellie Barnes <ellie@clearline.health>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:42:00Z
Subject: Internal: preliminary findings + immediate controls applied

Quick summary of what we observed between 07:45–08:20 UTC:
- Symptom: elevated per-token latency on streaming connections for a subset of connections belonging to Clearline. Non-streaming paths unaffected.
- Root hypothesis (prelim): routing amplification combined with aggressive autoscaler cooldowns — when many short-lived prefixes appeared, streaming shards experienced KV cache pressure and we'd see degraded tail latency as kernels reloaded.

Actions taken (09:20–09:35 UTC):
- Manually pinned Clearline traffic to a warm shard pool to reduce cross-tenant variance.
- Relaxed autoscaler cooldowns for streaming pools for 2 hours while we gather traces.
- Enabled a small rate-smoothing policy (server-side token pacing) for the pinned route to reduce burst output.

Customer impact: reduced token-level stalls; Ellie confirmed improved behavior when pinned route was active.

Next steps:
- Collect full traces and KV cache metrics (in progress).
- Prepare a short postmortem with timeline and permanent fix plan (target: 48–72 hours).
- Evaluate a runtime fix to make streaming shard handoffs idempotent and less sensitive to prefix churn.

Marcus
Lead Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Ellie Barnes <ellie@clearline.health>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-24T15:30:00Z
Subject: Post-incident recap: 2026-11-22 streaming delivery slowdown (Clearline Health)

Hi Ellie — thank you again for your patience. Below is a concise post-incident recap for the streaming slowdown you reported on 2026-11-22. Please let us know if you’d like a longer technical readout with graphs.

What happened
- Between ~07:40–08:25 UTC on 2026-11-22, certain streaming connections experienced intermittent token delivery stalls (10–30s). The non-streaming completion endpoint was not affected.

Root cause (finalized):
- A short-lived spike in unique request prefixes from Clearline’s workload increased prefix diversity on shared streaming shards. This caused repeated KV cache invalidations and kernel reloads during shard handoffs. The autoscaler cooldown settings then caused a small oscillation in available shard capacity, amplifying tail latency for streaming connections.

Why you saw it but not others
- Your workload pattern (many short messages with high prefix variance across operator sessions) created a worst-case surface for our streaming shard cache behavior.

Immediate mitigations performed
- Pinned Clearline to a warmed shard pool (reduced cross-tenant noise).
- Applied temporary server-side pacing to smooth token emission.
- Adjusted autoscaler cooldowns short term.

Permanent fixes planned
- Runtime change to make KV cache state transfers tolerant of high prefix churn (target: code rollout in 2 weeks, full validation in staging).
- Autoscaler tuning so shard capacity ramps without oscillation for short bursts (target: 1 week).
- New routing knob to allow per-tenant isolation for traffic patterns above an agree threshold (opt-in, target: 3 weeks).

Compensation and next steps
- We will apply a credit for any request cost incurred during the degradation window. Marcus will follow up with the precise credit amount and HubSpot ticket (HS-789213).
- I’ve scheduled a 30-minute walkthrough next Thursday 2026-11-30 at 16:00 UTC to review the fixes and answer questions — please let me know if that time works.

Attachments: postmortem-20261122.pdf (detailed timeline + graphs)

If you prefer we can keep your route pinned until the runtime change is validated — tell us and we’ll leave the control in place.

Apologies again for the disruption. We appreciate the signal and the quick logs you provided; they were critical to narrowing the scope.

—Kimberly
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
